title: The First Parliaments
objective: After this level you can explain how parliaments began in England and elsewhere.
summary: Kings needed consent for extra taxes, so councils grew into parliaments: León in 1188, the word in England by 1236, towns summoned in 1265, the Model Parliament of 1295 and a separate Commons in 1341.

cards.headline: Parliament began as a conversation. Its root is French parler, “to speak”.
cards.body: Kings didn’t set up parliaments out of kindness. They needed something only their subjects could hand over, and asking was the price.

cards.headline: A council gets a name
cards.body: In England the word parliament first turns up in 1236, for the king’s Great Council of great men. England wasn’t first, though. In 1188 the Spanish kingdom of León held an assembly where elected representatives of the towns sat with the king, the church and the nobles. UNESCO calls its decrees the oldest documentary evidence of Europe’s parliamentary system. Parliaments weren’t one country’s bright idea.

cards.headline: Money talks
cards.body: Here’s why they caught on. Wars cost more than a king could pay from his own wealth. Edward I and the kings after him needed extra taxes, and they needed Parliament’s agreement to raise them. Remember Level 71? Magna Carta itself had been reissued in 1225 in exchange for a new tax. Ask people for money often enough, and they start asking for things back.

cards.headline: Who got a seat
cards.body: In 1265 Simon de Montfort, rebelling against Henry III, summoned a parliament that for the first time included representatives of both counties and towns. Edward I’s Model Parliament of 1295 made it the pattern: nobles and bishops, plus two knights from each county and two burgesses from each town. In 1341 the knights and burgesses met separately for the first time, forming what became the House of Commons. Two rooms, and the start of two houses.

mascot.line: Two knights from every county, two burgesses from every town. The House of Commons started as a very long guest list.

cards.headline: The first parliaments: known
learned: Parliament comes from French parler, “to speak”
León’s assembly of 1188 included town representatives
Kings needed Parliament’s consent for extra taxes
1265: towns summoned; 1295: Model Parliament; 1341: Commons apart

questions.prompt: Who was first to summon representatives of both counties and towns to an English parliament, in 1265?

options.label: King Edward I, in his Model Parliament
options.rationale: He made it the pattern in 1295.

options.label: King Henry II, founder of the juries

questions.explanation: In 1265 Simon de Montfort, in rebellion against Henry III, summoned representatives of both counties and towns.

questions.prompt: Why did medieval English kings keep calling parliaments together?

options.label: They needed it to elect each new king of England
They wanted it to turn the Bible into English law
options.rationale: Parliament was about money and government.

options.label: They needed its agreement for extra taxes to pay for wars
The Pope ordered them to hold one every year
options.rationale: The push came from the kings’ own need for money.

questions.explanation: Wars cost more than kings could pay themselves, so they needed Parliament’s assent to extraordinary taxes.

questions.prompt: Parliaments grew from a bargain over taxes. How had Magna Carta’s 1225 reissue shown the same bargain?

options.label: Henry III granted it in exchange for a new tax
The barons paid the Pope to cancel it
options.rationale: The Pope annulled it in 1215, at John’s request.

options.label: The towns bought it from King John
options.rationale: The 1225 reissue came under Henry III.

options.label: It abolished all royal taxes
options.rationale: It was traded for a tax, not against taxes.

questions.explanation: In 1225 the charter was reissued in exchange for a new tax: rights for money, the same deal that drove parliaments.
